newsitem.title: UK: OPTIONS - Puts bought in Land Securities.
newsitem.headline: OPTIONS - Puts bought in Land Securities.

text.p: UK equity options were sparsely traded on Monday, reflecting the market's uncertainty ahead of the national elections on May 1 and of the near-term direction of Wall Street, dealers said.
The biggest deal in property company Land Securities was from a buyer of 400 October 700 puts at 6p and 6-1/2p which will make money if the underlying shares fall sufficiently.
By 1250 GMT, the shares had lost 2-1/2p to 785p.
In contrast, over in building materials group Redland the chief deal was from a buyer of 300 May 360 calls at 7p. Redland shares added 1/2p to 354-1/2p.
A bullish calendar spread was the main deal in communications services group Cable & Wireless from the sale of 150 July 550 calls at 4p and the purchase of 150 October 550 calls at 12p.

This is effectively an attempt to buy the October calls for 8p and therefore requires the underlying shares to stay below 550p by July expiry when these options will be worthless. The shares then need to rise above 508p by October expiry in order to make this a profitable strategy.
In index options one of the larger deals was a bear spread in European style FTSE options.

The spread was established by selling 500 June 4225 puts at 43p and buying 500 June 4325 puts at 70p for a net debit of 27p and it will make a maximum profit of 73p if the FTSE falls below 4225 by expiry.
In American style FTSE, one of the larger deals was from a buyer of 500 June 4600 calls at 20-1/2p who also sold June FTSE futures at 4395 in a volatility trade.
At 1250 GMT, spot FTSE was up 7.6 at 4377.3 while June futures were up four points at 4398.
